# C++ control codec goldens

These files are verbatim output from LegacyClonk's C++ binary serializers. They
are inputs to Rust decode/re-encode tests; they must never be generated by the
Rust codec itself.

## Provenance

- Generator revision: `5b9f1d13d4d62e5685f6dc4024180e0fc9079804`
- Revision signature: verified with `git verify-commit` (Tyler Ashworth,
  RSA `77C5A13029790F43202F4B09D655945BC5403E07`)
- Generator build: unmodified detached checkout, Debug,
  `USE_RUST_ENGINE_VALIDATION=ON`
- Generator executable SHA-256:
  `df08ae1a2f1e5cb126db0228349207e67879d94dd444fb1bebf47e24c9cd07c5`
- Platform: `aarch64-apple-darwin`, little-endian
- Generation date: 2026-07-20

That revision contains three test-only command-line wrappers. Each wrapper
parses the named INI fixture and delegates to the production C++ serializer:

- `C4PacketControlPkt` with `StdCompilerBinWrite`
- `C4PacketPlayerInfoUpdRequest::pack(PID_PlayerInfoUpdReq)`
- `C4GameControlPacket::Set` with `StdCompilerBinWrite`

The wrappers do not construct packet bytes themselves. At generation time, the
relevant production serializer files were byte-identical between the generator
revision and adoption base revision
`9305e6d8db7ac2ddd83d42cf286c029d62f0f8e7`:

`C4Control.cpp`, `C4PlayerInfo.cpp`, `C4Network2Res.cpp`,
`C4Network2IO.cpp`, `C4GameControlNetwork.cpp`, `StdCompiler.cpp`,
`StdAdaptors.h`, `C4Client.cpp`, `C4PacketBase.h`, and `C4Packet2.cpp`.

Nine input INI files are also byte-identical to the generator revision.
`synchronize.ini` was added later and was passed to the generator's generic
single-control wrapper.

Every output was generated twice in separate directories and compared
byte-for-byte before being checked in.

## Inputs and commands

Run these from `rust/crates/clonk-network/tests/fixtures`, replacing `<oracle>`
with an executable built from the generator revision and `<out>` with the
destination directory.

```text
<oracle> --control-packet-codec-oracle 1 synchronize.ini <out>/synchronize_delivery_1.bin
<oracle> --control-packet-codec-oracle 1 client_update_activate.ini <out>/client_update_activate_delivery_1.bin
<oracle> --control-packet-codec-oracle 2 client_join.ini <out>/client_join_delivery_2.bin
<oracle> --control-packet-codec-oracle 1 client_remove.ini <out>/client_remove_delivery_1.bin
<oracle> --player-info-update-codec-oracle player_info_update_request_add.ini <out>/player_info_update_request_add.bin
<oracle> --control-packet-codec-oracle 2 player_info_minimal.ini <out>/player_info_minimal_delivery_2.bin
<oracle> --control-codec-oracle 4 64 join_player_embedded.ini <out>/join_player_embedded_client_4_tick_64.bin
<oracle> --control-codec-oracle 4 7 player_info_minimal.ini <out>/player_info_minimal_client_4_tick_7.bin
<oracle> --control-codec-oracle 4 7 join_player_resource.ini <out>/join_player_resource_client_4_tick_7.bin
<oracle> --control-codec-oracle 4 7 join_player_resource_sha.ini <out>/join_player_resource_sha_client_4_tick_7.bin
<oracle> --control-codec-oracle 4 7 player_info_resource.ini <out>/player_info_resource_client_4_tick_7.bin
```

The C++ and Rust codecs intentionally use native-endian fixed-width integers.
These goldens therefore cover supported little-endian targets. A big-endian
port needs a separately generated C++ fixture set.
